name: ESL MPSoC tile / bus architecture block
author: cp-4856 PoC graft (grounded in tsarilp-pub doc/common/tikzsetup.tex, not a fork of that file)
description: MPSoC-style tile/bus architecture figure: per-tile Core + Accelerator + config-register block joined by an intra-tile bus, two tiles joined by a dashed inter-tile NoC bus through a shared I/O terminal node. Colors are the ESL domain-semantic tokens (contract §2, ADR-0005 D7): core-accent=core/compute (Aquamarine), process-accent=datapath/accelerator (NavyBlue), param-accent=config/parameters (ForestGreen), intra-bus=Orange, inter-bus=NavyBlue, digitaldomain=terminal/IO (gray) -- extending opentikz's five-color ot* palette, not remapped onto it (see reference/color-palettes/color-palettes.md and cp-4856 learnings note on the palette-invariant collision).

parameters.name: \tilesep
parameters.meaning: horizontal gap between the two tile boundary boxes

parameters.name: \cfgonelabel
parameters.meaning: tile 0 config-register block label (use \\ for two lines)

parameters.name: \cfgtwolabel
parameters.meaning: tile 1 config-register block label (use \\ for two lines)

parameters.name: \interbuslabel
parameters.meaning: inter-tile bus caption above the I/O node

edit_contract.node_naming: fixed semantic node names: (core1) (acc1) (cfg1) (tile1) (core2) (acc2) (cfg2) (tile2) (io); new per-tile components take a role-based name with the tile-index suffix (e.g. (mem1), (dma2))

operations.summary: declare a node inside the tile with a role style (core/process/parameters), position it relative to an existing tile-local node, connect it with intrabus, then add it to that tile's fit=(...) list so the boundary re-encloses it

duplicate a tile's node block with a fresh index (3, 4, ...), position its fit node right=\tilesep cm of the previous tile, wire the shared io node to the new tile's fit.north, and extend the coordinate used for the interbus caption if more than two tiles are joined at the io hub

swap a node's style to change its role: core<->process<->parameters; each role keeps its own dedicated palette color per the domain-semantic scheme, so a role change also changes the color, never just the shape
adjust the tile's fit margins={left=...,right=...,top=...,bottom=...} values (grafted tikzsetup.tex pgfkeys helper) or extend which nodes are in its fit=(...) list

change the domain-semantic color for a whole role by re-binding that role's palette token (e.g. \colorlet{core-accent}{...}), never by editing the role's style to a raw color; keep intrabus=intra-bus, interbus=inter-bus-dashed, core=core-accent, process=process-accent, parameters=param-accent unless the family's settled-decisions record says otherwise (see cp-4856 note: this template has no settled-decisions record of its own yet — it is a PoC graft, not the shipped Phase-1 component library)

invariants: each tile's boundary fit node must be declared after all nodes it fits, inside an on-background-layer scope, so it sits behind them
preserve semantic node names; give new components clear role-based names with a tile-index suffix

colors encode role/domain semantics (core/process/parameters/terminal/intrabus/interbus) via the contract §2 palette tokens (core-accent/process-accent/param-accent/digitaldomain/intra-bus/inter-bus), not decoration — do not introduce a raw hex or stock xcolor/dvipsnames name (tools/validate.py rejects this), and do not force these roles onto opentikz's otblue/otorange/otteal/otpurple/otgray names (palette collision — see learnings note; ADR-0005 D7 extends the palette instead)

the inter-tile bus is always dashed and the intra-tile bus is always solid — this distinction is load-bearing (NoC/global vs. local/tile-internal), grafted from tikzsetup.tex's intrabus/interbus split
